title: Build enterprise generative AI apps using Llama 3 at 1,000 tokens/s on the SambaNova AI platform
talk_summary: SambaNova pitches its full-stack RDU platform and Composition of Experts for fast Llama 3 inference, with a single endpoint that routes prompts to expert models and supports model chaining. The hands-on section builds a basic Llama 3 API call and a RAG Q&A app using LangChain, E5 embeddings, Chroma, and chunking/retrieval.

takeaways.what_they_do: A single endpoint routes an incoming prompt to the best-suited expert model behind the scenes, while also allowing direct model calls and chaining.
takeaways.evidence_quote: determine based off of an incoming prompt what is the best suited expert behind the scenes to solve that prompt

takeaways.what_they_do: Model-level RBAC restricts which applications, people, or groups can access each model behind the shared endpoint.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this application or this person or this group of people should be able to access this set of models

takeaways.technique: RAG with chunking, embeddings, and reranker
takeaways.what_they_do: Documents are loaded, split into chunks, embedded into a vector store, retrieved by similarity, and optionally reranked before being passed to the LLM.
takeaways.numbers: chunk size 1200, overlap 240; 15-page PDF -> 89 chunks; top K 3; embedding took 4 seconds

takeaways.what_they_do: Open-source Llama 3 needs explicit BOS/user/assistant special tags; without them the model adds unasked content or answers poorly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to let the llm know that this is the beginning of text and this is where you will insert the user query

takeaways.what_they_do: The platform supports routing, direct model calls, and chaining models together for agentic workflows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: with agentic AI you may need to do model chaining
